name: Ordering a Ride or Food with Apps (Uber, Lyft, DoorDash)
objectives: Using the official app store, install a ride app, make an account and add a payment method safely, with the developer checked and card details typed only inside the app
Given a pickup and a destination, enter both in a ride app and read the price and arrival time before you confirm, with the pickup spot checked on the map and the price read before booking

When a booked car arrives, check the plate, car and driver against the app and find the safety tools, never getting into a car that does not match and finding Share My Trip, the emergency button and the PIN
Using a delivery app, enter your delivery address with notes and build an order in the cart, with the full address, a helpful note and a choice for out-of-stock items
Given a checkout screen, explain each line, including the item total, fees, tip and total, before you pay, naming every charge correctly and checking the total against your budget
After a ride or delivery, check the receipt, get help for a problem inside the app and refuse fake support, using only the in-app Help and never giving a password or code

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Setting up a ride app
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Install a ride app, make an account and add a payment method safely.
This lesson builds toward: Using the official app store, you will install a ride app, make an account and add a payment method safely, with the developer checked and card details typed only inside the app.
Uber and Lyft are the best-known ride apps in the United States. A driver uses their own car to take you where you want to go, and you pay through the app.
Install the app only from the official app store (Google Play or the App Store) and check the developer is Uber or Lyft. Sign up with your phone number and email. Uber's terms say you must be 18 or older for your own account; teens 13 to 17 can only ride through a teen account a parent or guardian sets up. Check the app's own terms for the current rules.
Add a payment method inside the app, such as a debit or credit card. Type it only in the app, never in a text or email. Add your home as a saved place so it is quick to choose later.
Step by step:
- Open the official app store and search for Uber or Lyft.
- Check the developer name, then install.
- Sign up with your phone number and email.
- Add a payment method inside the app's payment or wallet section.
- Save your home address as a saved place.
Words to know:
- Ride app: an app that sends a driver in their own car to pick you up.
- Payment method: the card or account the app charges.
- Saved place: an address the app remembers, like home.
Official sources:
- Uber: US Terms of Use (age and teen accounts)
Try it now: Install Uber or Lyft from the official app store, create your account, and save your home address. You can wait to add a card until you need a ride.
You can now install a ride app safely, create an account and save your home address.

check.q: In a ride app, who drives the car?
options: A driver using their own car
check.why: A driver uses their own car to take you, and you pay through the app.

check.q: A text asks you to reply with your card number to finish setting up your ride account. What would you do?
options: Ignore it and add the card only inside the official app
Call the number in the text and read it out
check.why: Type your card details only in the app, never in a text or email.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Requesting a ride and seeing the price first
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Enter a pickup and destination and read the price before you confirm.
This lesson builds toward: Given a pickup and a destination, you will enter both in a ride app and read the price and arrival time before you confirm, with the pickup spot checked on the map and the price read before booking.
Open the app and type where you want to go in the "Where to?" box. Check the pickup spot: the app uses your location, but you can move the pin or type the address so the driver finds you.
The app shows ride choices, from cheaper shared or standard rides to bigger or nicer cars, each with a price and an arrival time. The price can be higher at busy times, such as rush hour or after a big event.
Choose the ride, check the price and payment method, and confirm. Then the app shows the driver's name, photo, car and license plate, and a map of the car coming to you.
Step by step:
- Type your destination in the "Where to?" box.
- Check the pickup spot; move the pin if needed.
- Compare ride choices: price and arrival time.
- Check the payment method.
- Confirm only when the price is OK.
- Watch the map for your car.
Words to know:
- Pickup spot: where the driver will meet you.
- Destination: where you want to go.
- Busy-time pricing: higher prices when many people want rides at once.
Try it now: Open the ride app and type a real destination, like a clinic, library or job center. Read two ride choices and their prices. Close the app without booking unless you need the ride.
You can now request a ride and read the price and arrival time before you agree.

check.q: What does the app show you after you confirm a ride?
options: The driver's name, photo, car and license plate
check.why: After you confirm, the app shows the driver, car and plate, and a map.

check.q: The app put your pickup pin across a busy road from where you stand. What would you do?
options: Book anyway and run across the road
Move the pin or type the address so the driver finds you
check.why: You can move the pin or type the address so the pickup spot is right.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Getting in the right car, safely
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Check the car, plate and driver before getting in, and use the safety tools.
This lesson builds toward: When a booked car arrives, you will check the plate, car and driver against the app and find the safety tools, never getting into a car that does not match and finding Share My Trip, the emergency button and the PIN.
Before you get in, check three things against the app: the license plate, the car's make and color, and the driver's name and photo. Ask "Who are you here for?" and let the driver say your name. If anything does not match, do not get in.
Uber has an optional four-digit PIN: you tell the driver the PIN, and the trip can only start with the right one. Uber's Share My Trip lets trusted family or friends follow your trip live, and its in-app emergency button contacts 911 and shows your location and car details. Lyft has its own safety tools; find them on its safety page or in the app.
Wait indoors until the app shows the car has arrived, and do not get into a car that offers you a ride without being booked in the app.
Step by step:
- Wait inside until the app says the car is here.
- Check the plate, car and driver's photo.
- Ask "Who are you here for?"
- Use the PIN if you turned it on.
- Share your trip with a family member or friend.
- Know where the emergency button is.
Words to know:
- License plate: the number plate on the car; check it matches the app.
- Share My Trip: Uber's tool that lets people you choose follow your ride live.
- PIN: a short number code you tell the driver to start the ride.
Official sources:
- Uber: Rider safety
Try it now: Open the safety section of your ride app. Find how to share a trip and where the emergency button is. If your app has a ride PIN, turn it on.
You can now check you have the right car and driver, and use the app's safety tools.

check.q: What does Uber's Share My Trip do?
options: Splits the price with a stranger
Lets trusted family or friends follow your trip live
Posts your trip on social media
check.why: Share My Trip lets people you trust follow your trip live.

check.q: A driver says "Are you Maria?" and you are Maria. What would you do instead of saying yes?
options: Tell the driver your PIN before checking anything
Ask "Who are you here for?" and let the driver say your name
check.why: Letting the driver say your name shows they really were sent for you.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Ordering a meal or groceries for delivery
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Find a restaurant or store in a delivery app and build an order.
This lesson builds toward: Using a delivery app, you will enter your delivery address with notes and build an order in the cart, with the full address, a helpful note and a choice for out-of-stock items.
Delivery apps like DoorDash, Uber Eats and Instacart let you order from local restaurants and stores. A delivery person, sometimes called a Dasher or shopper, picks up your order and brings it to you.
Install from the official app store and enter your delivery address carefully, with any apartment or gate number and notes for the driver, like "blue door, ring the bell".
Browse or search for a restaurant or store, tap items to add them to your cart, and choose options like size. For groceries, you can usually pick what the shopper should do if an item is out of stock: replace it with something similar, or refund it.
Step by step:
- Install the delivery app from the official store.
- Enter your full delivery address and notes for the driver.
- Search for a restaurant or store.
- Tap items to add them to your cart.
- For groceries, choose what to do if an item is out of stock.
Words to know:
- Delivery app: an app that brings food or goods from local businesses to your door.
- Cart: the list of items you plan to buy.
- Substitution: a similar item the shopper picks when yours is out of stock.
Try it now: Open a delivery app (install it from the official store if needed). Enter your address with a note for the driver, then add two items to a cart. Do not place the order yet.
You can now find a restaurant or store in a delivery app and build an order for your address.

check.q: In a delivery app, who brings your order?
options: A delivery person, sometimes called a Dasher or shopper
check.why: A delivery person picks up your order and brings it to you.

check.q: You live in apartment 4B behind a gate. What would you do when you enter your address?
options: Add the apartment number, gate details and a note for the driver
check.why: Apartment and gate numbers and a note help the driver find you.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Understanding the checkout: fees, tips and total
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Read the checkout screen and know what each charge is before you pay.
This lesson builds toward: Given a checkout screen, you will explain each line, including the item total, fees, tip and total, before you pay, naming every charge correctly and checking the total against your budget.
The price on the menu is not the whole cost. The checkout screen lists the item total plus extra charges, which can include a delivery fee, a service fee, sometimes a small-order fee, taxes, and a tip for the driver.
Fees change by app, time, distance and city, and some apps offer paid memberships that lower fees. So always read the checkout screen and look at the total before you tap Place order.
The tip goes to the driver or shopper. You choose the amount, and many apps let you change it after delivery. If the total is more than you planned, remove an item or choose pickup instead of delivery if the app offers it.
Step by step:
- Open your cart and go to checkout.
- Read each line: items, delivery fee, service fee, taxes, tip.
- Check the delivery address and payment method.
- Look at the total.
- Change the order or tip if needed, then tap Place order.
Words to know:
- Delivery fee: a charge for bringing the order to you.
- Service fee: a charge the app adds for using its service.
- Tip: money you choose to give the driver or shopper.
Try it now: Take the cart from the last lesson to the checkout screen. Write down the item total, each fee, the tip and the final total. Then decide whether to place it or close the app.
You can now read a delivery checkout screen and know the full cost before you pay.

check.q: Who receives the tip on a delivery order?
check.why: The tip goes to the driver or shopper.

check.q: Your menu items add up to a small amount, but the total is much higher. What would you do before placing the order?
options: Add more items to make it worth it
Read each line on the checkout screen to see the fees, taxes and tip
Close the app and pay by gift card
check.why: The checkout screen lists every fee, the tax and the tip that make up the total.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Receipts, problems and staying safe
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Check a receipt, get help with a wrong order and avoid app scams.
This lesson builds toward: After a ride or delivery, you will check the receipt, get help for a problem inside the app and refuse fake support, using only the in-app Help and never giving a password or code.
After a ride or delivery, the app sends a receipt to your email and keeps it in the app under your trips or orders. Check that the charge matches what you agreed.
If something is wrong, like a missing item, a cold meal or a wrong charge, use the Help or Support section inside the app and choose the order. Report problems soon after they happen.
Scammers pretend to be app support. Real help is in the app. Do not call a support number from a search ad, and never give your password or a code sent to your phone to anyone who calls or texts you. Pay only inside the app, not in cash or gift cards to someone who asks.
Step by step:
- Open your trips or orders in the app.
- Check the receipt matches what you agreed.
- For a problem, go to Help inside the app and pick the order.
- Never give a password or a phone code to a caller.
- Pay only inside the app.
Words to know:
- Receipt: a record of what you paid and for what.
- Support: the help section of the app for problems.
Try it now: Final task practice: open the trips or orders section of your ride or delivery app and find the Help area. Then do the final task: price a ride and find the safety tools, and read a full delivery checkout screen.
You can now check a receipt, get help for a problem inside the app, and avoid fake support scams.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Price before booking The pickup or destination is wrong, or the price and arrival time were not read. A real pickup and destination are entered, and the price and arrival time are read before any booking. Also compares two ride choices and says why the price may be higher at busy times. Safety tools Cannot find the safety tools. Finds Share My Trip, the emergency button and the ride PIN (or the app's own safety tools). Also explains the three checks before getting into the car. Delivery order The cart is empty or the delivery address is incomplete. A small order in the cart with a full delivery address. Adds a helpful note for the driver and a choice for out-of-stock items. Reading the checkout Cannot say what the fees, tip or total are. Explains the item total, each fee, the tip, the delivery address and the total. Also names one way to lower the total, such as removing an item or choosing pickup. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: Where can you find a receipt for a delivery?
options: In your email and in the app under your orders
Nowhere; apps do not give receipts
check.why: The app emails a receipt and keeps it under your trips or orders.

check.q: Your food never arrived and you search online for the app's support number. An ad shows a phone number. What would you do?
options: Call the number from the ad
Pay a stranger in gift cards for a refund
Skip the ad and use Help inside the app
check.why: Real help is in the app; support numbers in search ads can be scammers.
